content: It belongs to a class of drugs known as mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists. Eplerenone is available in tablet form and is taken orally, typically once or twice daily. It can be taken with or without food. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. It is important to take eplerenone exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Your doctor may start you on a low dose and gradually increase it after four weeks. It may take four weeks or longer to experience the full benefits of the medication. Continue taking eplerenone even if you feel well, and do not stop using it without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes. If you have questions about additional uses, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Before starting eplerenone, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to eplerenone or any other medications. Do not take eplerenone if you are currently using certain medications, including amiloride, amiloride with hydrochlorothiazide, itraconazole, ketoconazole, potassium supplements, spironolactone, spironolactone with hydrochlorothiazide, triamterene, or triamterene with hydrochlorothiazide. Additionally, provide your doctor with a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking.g., benazepril, captopril, enalapril, fosinopril, lisinopril, quinapril), angiotensin II receptor antagonists (e.g., eprosartan, irbesartan, losartan, olmesartan, valsartan), NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen), cimetidine, clarithromycin, danazol, delavirdine, diltiazem, erythromycin, fluconazole, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, HIV protease inhibitors (e.g., indinavir, ritonavir, saquinavir), isoniazid, lithium, metronidazole, nefazodone, troleandomycin, verapamil, and zafirlukast. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Inform your doctor if you are using herbal products, particularly St. John’s wort. Additionally, disclose if you have or have ever had high potassium levels, diabetes, gout, or liver or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking eplerenone, contact your doctor immediately. Discuss with your doctor whether you can consume grapefruit juice while taking eplerenone. Avoid using potassium-containing salt substitutes while on this medication. If your doctor has recommended a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose of eplerenone, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Eplerenone may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: headache, dizziness, diarrhea, stomach pain, cough, excessive fatigue, flu-like symptoms, breast enlargement or tenderness, or abnormal vaginal bleeding. Some side effects can be serious. If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your doctor immediately: chest pain, tingling in the arms or legs, loss of muscle tone, weakness or heaviness in the legs, confusion, lack of energy, cold or gray skin, or an irregular heartbeat. If you notice any unusual problems while taking eplerenone, inform your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store eplerenone in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Symptoms of overdose may include fainting, dizziness, blurred vision, upset stomach, tingling in the arms or legs, loss of muscle tone, weakness or heaviness in the legs, confusion, lack of energy, cold or gray skin, or an irregular or slow heartbeat. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Eplerenone is sold under the brand name Inspra®.
